data.description:
## Context / Problem
The RP-03 epic (4217-d1d6) carries a REQUIRED acceptance criterion: a Live External Integration workflow must run GREEN in GitHub Actions, fully exercising the coordinator's create / binding-lifecycle mutation paths end-to-end against BOTH a live Jira Cloud instance and a live Jira Data Center instance, with real transports and credentials. The DC half is satisfied by the ephemeral Dockerized `jira-dc-harness` (real create/update/assign/label/link round-trips). The Cloud half is NOT: the only Cloud lane (`jira-cloud-s3-rehearsal`) is deliberately read-only against the shared production instance.

rebar already ships a bounded, self-cleaning live-Cloud mutation probe — `rebar bridge check-access` (`access_check.run_access_check`) — which creates a uniquely-labeled throwaway issue, adds a label, writes+reads an entity property, JQL-searches for it, and ALWAYS deletes it in a `finally` (verified live against REB: CREATE/LABEL/PROPERTY_WRITE/PROPERTY_READ/DELETE all pass; the issue is cleaned up even on a mid-probe failure). Its one weakness against real Cloud is the `STEP_JQL_SEARCH` step: the retry budget is a fixed `JQL_RETRY_COUNT=6 x JQL_RETRY_SLEEP=5s` with no backoff, which is shorter than Jira Cloud's search-index eventual-consistency lag, so the step flakes `no_results_after_retry` even though the write demonstrably landed (the immediately-following by-key property read passes).

## Outcome
1. Make the probe's JQL-visibility step robust to Cloud search-index lag by root-causing the flake: add exponential backoff and raise the budget, both env-tunable (`JIRA_PROBE_JQL_RETRIES`, `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_SLEEP`) so CI can tune without a code change, with a safe default that covers observed REB lag. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged; the probe still always deletes.
2. Add a self-cleaning MUTATING live-Cloud lane to `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` that (a) runs `rebar bridge preview` as a dry-run forecast, then (b) runs `rebar bridge check-access` against the live REB project (real create/modify/delete), gating the job GREEN, and (c) on failure/cancel runs a label-sweep teardown backstop that deletes any leaked `rebar-id:` probe issue.

This makes the Live External Integration workflow genuinely exercise live Cloud mutation, satisfying the epic's Cloud AC with real transport + credentials, at bounded, reversible, self-cleaning cost.

## Plan
1. In `access_check.run_access_check`, extract the JQL-search retry into a small helper that reads the retry count and base sleep from env (falling back to the module defaults), and sleeps with exponential backoff (`base * 2**attempt`, capped) between attempts via the injected `sleep_fn`. Raise the default budget to cover observed REB lag. No change to create/label/property/delete ordering or to the always-delete `finally`.
2. Add a `jira-cloud-mutation-probe` job to `external-integration.yml`, modeled on the existing Cloud lane's auth/setup steps (acli install + `acli jira auth login`, JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_PROJECT vars + JIRA_API_TOKEN secret), that runs `rebar bridge preview` then `rebar bridge check-access`, with an `if: failure() || cancelled()` teardown step that lists+deletes leftover `labels ~ "rebar-id:"` issues. Gate it behind the live-Jira credential vars so it no-ops cleanly when unset (portable: no dependence on any single CI provider — the same `rebar bridge check-access` command is the operation-linked fallback runnable locally).
3. Document the lane and its safety model (bounded, uniquely-labeled, always-deleted, dry-run-forecast-first) in `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/README.md` (or a sibling README) so the read-only vs mutating Cloud distinction is explicit.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- A unit test drives `run_access_check` with a fake client whose `search_issues` returns `[]` for the first N attempts then a hit, and a recording `sleep_fn`; it asserts (a) the probe PASSES (verdict PASS, exit 0) when the hit arrives within the (raised/backoff) budget, and (b) the recorded sleeps follow exponential backoff. RED first: with the current fixed-sleep/low-budget code the assertions on backoff and on tolerating a longer lag fail.
- A unit test asserts the env overrides (`JIRA_PROBE_JQL_RETRIES`/`JIRA_PROBE_JQL_SLEEP`) change the effective budget.
- A regression test asserts the issue is ALWAYS deleted (STEP_DELETE present + passed) even when the JQL step fails, using a fake whose search never returns — pinning the self-cleaning invariant.
- A workflow-lint/structure test (mirroring existing `tests/.../test_*workflow*` if present) asserts the new job exists, runs `bridge check-access`, and has the failure-teardown sweep step.

## Compatibility / rollback
Additive: a new CI job + an env-tunable retry budget with unchanged defaults-behaviour semantics (only the default numbers grow and gain backoff). No stored-format, API, or CLI-contract change. Rollback is a code revert; nothing persists in Jira (every probe issue is deleted) and no store state is written.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `run_access_check`'s JQL-visibility step uses exponential backoff and an env-tunable budget (`JIRA_PROBE_JQL_RETRIES`, `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_SLEEP`) with a default that tolerates observed REB Cloud index lag; unit tests cover the backoff schedule and the env overrides (RED-first).
- [ ] The probe still ALWAYS deletes its throwaway issue on every path (including JQL-step failure), pinned by a regression test.
- [ ] `external-integration.yml` has a `jira-cloud-mutation-probe` job that runs `rebar bridge preview` (dry-run) then `rebar bridge check-access` against live REB, gated behind the live-Jira credential vars, with a failure/cancel label-sweep teardown backstop.
- [ ] The lane's bounded self-cleaning safety model is documented, and the read-only vs mutating Cloud distinction is explicit.
- [ ] A dispatched Live External Integration run shows the new Cloud-mutation lane GREEN alongside the existing DC-mutation lane (real transport + credentials).
- [ ] Portability: the live-Cloud mutation capability is exercised by the `rebar bridge check-access` operation itself (runnable locally / under any CI), not solely by a GitHub-Actions-specific trigger.
data.title: RP-03: self-cleaning mutating live-Cloud integration lane (robust JQL probe + workflow job)
